publications.abstract: Frames from overlapping thermal sensors are merged on a server into one room image before counting.
publications.description: Two or more thermal sensors with overlapping fields of view stream their frames to a building server. The server registers the frames to a common floor grid, merges them into one thermal image of the room, and counts people in the merged image so that a person in the overlap is counted once.

independent_claims.quote: A system comprising a plurality of thermal sensors with overlapping fields of view and a server configured to receive frames from each sensor, register the frames to a common grid, merge the registered frames into a single room image, and count persons in the single room image.

publications.title: Merging overlapping thermal sensor views for room counting

publications.abstract: Sensors send counts, not images; a controller subtracts the overlap count.

dependent_claims.quote: The method of claim 1, wherein each sensor updates a background estimate only while no motion has been detected for a holding period.

publications.description: Each sensor processes its frames locally and transmits only a count of persons and a count of persons inside a predefined overlap region. A room controller computes the room count as the sum of the sensor counts minus the overlap count. Each sensor updates its background only while no motion has been detected for a holding period.

independent_claims.quote: A method of counting occupants of a room monitored by a first sensor and a second sensor with an overlap region, comprising: at each sensor, counting persons locally and counting persons within the overlap region; transmitting only the counts; and computing a room count as the sum of the counts minus the overlap count.

publications.title: Privacy-preserving occupancy counting across overlapping sensors
